# Apple Computer_ Welcome To Macintosh (1989)

**Source**: /Volumes/NvME-Satechi/steve-jobs.ai/Database_Steve_Jobs/1980s/Apple Computer_ Welcome To Macintosh (1989).mp4

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-31 10:04

---

**Speaker 1**: They seemed rather upset.

**Speaker 2**: He said, no, I've got an MS-DOS machine at home. I'd much more prefer to keep with the MS-DOS type computer. And I said, no, Jim, once you get a Macintosh and work with it for one day, I said, you'll see that you want the Macintosh. And that's that's happened.

**Speaker 3**: The first time I turned on the machine, it was a real eye-opener to me because uh it was so simple the way the thing worked. Uh you could just look at the screen and even without any instruction, you could basically understand how to do it.

**Speaker 4**: You realize, you know, that you're doing the same thing on the Mac that you were doing by doing star.star copy to blah blah blah blah blah. You do it instead with your finger and a little pointer and a click of the mouse and a pull down of the menu.

**Speaker 5**: All you do is take this little mouse, which is a little device connected to to the machine and you point it and there's a cursor basically moves around the screen to what you want.

**Speaker 6**: When that realization finally gets through to that user, I imagine they go, "Ah."

**Speaker 7**: They look at the trash can, for instance. The first time you throw something in the trash can, people just laugh. I mean, it it happens over and over again. They think that's the the greatest thing.

**Speaker 8**: If you want to throw something away, you just pull it down into the trash can.

**Speaker 9**: One simply grabs it with a mouse, drags it to the trash can.

**Speaker 10**: And it goes. That's right.

**Speaker 9**: That's it.

**Speaker 11**: I think the supreme compliment is the fact that I don't have to worry about that stuff. How do I copy a file and how do I move it from here to there and and those things are just not the issue with the Mac because they're so easy.

**Speaker 12**: It's very intuitive. I can manage my hard disk. I can keep track of where things are because of the way this desktop is designed.

**Speaker 13**: I could begin word processing immediately. I didn't have to go into a whole series of trying to learn how to do it. In fact, I was turning out reports the same day I started using the Macintosh.

**Speaker 14**: If you sit down for a couple hours, take the book and go step by step, you can learn it in those couple hours. You know, once you learn all the commands, it it applies almost every program that they have.

**Speaker 15**: You can move very easily between a word processing program, to a spreadsheet program, to a database program with a very short learning curve.

**Speaker 16**: With a Macintosh, the machine doesn't control you, I control it.

**Speaker 17**: I had four of them wired up and singing Stand By Me Acapella. That was real good.

**Speaker 18**: At Federal Express, I believe you can go to just about anybody that has a Macintosh sitting on their desk and they'll tell you that that Macintosh is doing the work of two or sometimes three people.

**Speaker 19**: When you walk in your office, there's nobody there. When you turn that Mac on, it's like you have an assistant with you. Without and the assistant doesn't say anything, it just works for you.

**Speaker 20**: You can put a brand new person down with a brand new Macintosh and in one week's time, he's productive on it. It doesn't take a lot of training. It doesn't take a lot of programming skills.

**Speaker 21**: Leanne, write me a memo. I'll be able to respond right from my desk without a phone call interruption. I can answer her message whenever I want to while I'm working on the report and a memo while I'm in my mainframe.

**Speaker 22**: You could be working in a graphics program and quite easily flip over to a word processing program, import or export information from a database or even go to a mainframe application and gather information and go back to your original document all within the same screen by just clicking the mouse. If you remove those Macintoshes from Federal Express today, the work and the productivity and the credibility that is being maintained in each department would quite literally cease to exist.

**Speaker 23**: Blue Cross of California is the largest health insurer in the state of California. And of course, what we do is we provide individuals, uh groups and businesses with a variety of highly tailored uh health insurance plans.

**Speaker 24**: In most companies, the Macs come in the back door and and funnel up. But here at Blue Cross, it's it's been the opposite situation. They've actually been mandated to be the standard by uh a very high level of the company.

**Speaker 23**: Once they started coming in, people around them saw how those who were using Macintoshes were solving their business problems.

**Speaker 24**: And they wanted one for their desk. Many of the newer applications in the MS-DOS area, the ones that we're most interested in, the power applications, can't run on the bulk of our equipment without very expensive modification or having to buy new equipment. In fact, we're we're finding that more and more often is the case. Uh and yet with the Macintosh, clear across the range, I can go ahead and use the same software applications all the way from the Mac SE, which is our low-end machine, all the way up to the new 2CX, which is our new standard high-end machine. And that's simply not true in the MS-DOS world. And I think it uh it could potentially be a problem within OS/2 itself.

**Speaker 25**: US West Direct publishes the Yellow Pages for Mountain Bell, uh Pacific Northwest Bell and Pacific Bell. And we were doing little yellow page ads and that type of thing. It was great. But uh I quickly realized that I could do a lot more with it than draw ads. And that's really where it kind of took off. Uh at that point, my regional vice president came down and saw what I was doing and said, well, this is great. Uh and it just kept going on and she says, well, can you do this for the whole office maybe? I said, sure. Why not? And then this came completely out of the blue. It was suggested that uh um we might want to use this program to track sales for all of US West Direct. And uh that kind of blew my mind a little bit. I thought, well, yeah, this is great. We can do this. So now we are set up in um 30 offices across the United States with relational multi-user remote hooked up networks. Um which is pretty complicated stuff. It's simple, but the sophistication is there. I think that's the part of it that um really gets people excited because you can get past that layer of technically how do I use this machine and how do I get it to do that and you can start concentrating on all the wonderful things that it can do.

**Speaker 26**: Pizza Hut is the largest pizza chain in the world. And our sales volume puts us third in the food service industry just behind McDonald's and Burger King.

**Speaker 27**: In MIS, we like to keep things very simple. And that means we've got one computer platform. By doing that, maintenance is easy, training is easy. This is all there is. However, sometimes there's an overwhelming reason to get another computer platform. And that happened on the Macintosh.

**Speaker 28**: We had people that would not touch a computer. When we got the Mac in, those people got into that computer and within a day, they were using it and they weren't afraid of it any longer.

**Speaker 29**: One of the driving factors that has put the Macintosh in the forefront is the ability to uh use electronic mail. We put Microsoft Mail on the system and I simply send a message over to some co-worker and say, can you give me this information? At their convenience, they respond to it. At their convenience, they send me the response back. By the end of the day, I have my answer. Literally, hours are saved every day because we have that email system.

**Speaker 30**: You have faster communications, you have better quality preparation of data, of graphs. You can do analysis, you can do beautiful charts and graphs if you need them. What it what it does is is gives you a sense that you're going to be able to act.

**Speaker 31**: At some point, and it's almost magical when you see it happen, these people are sitting there working away and it becomes second nature. The mouse is there, the keyboard is there, but they've taken the machine, it's become part of them. It is no longer an adversary, it is simply a support tool that they can use. And at that point, the Macintosh is doing what it's supposed to do.

**Speaker 32**: You get real dependent on your Macintosh because it becomes an extension of your own personality. People want to dress up the desktop and name it little names and and it's, you know, it's part of you.

**Speaker 33**: Now, um I I look at the machine as just a part of what I am. It's a part of what I do every day. As a matter of fact, I couldn't imagine not using the machine trying to get any work done because I use it for so many different things.

**Speaker 34**: It's like being a child again when you go ahead and find the the the new things that you can do with this machine to go ahead and make your own work more effective, more productive and more professional.

**Speaker 35**: So I'm still able to do my job. I'm just able to do it easier and faster without the frustrations that I felt before.

**Speaker 36**: There have been instances where because of realignments, a person's assigned to a new area. And unfortunately, when they get there, they no longer have the Mac on their desk, they've got an IBM. Uh it's it's a big problem.

**Speaker 37**: If somebody tried to take this away from me, I'd cut off their arm, I think.

**Speaker 38**: Nobody gives them up willingly.
